title: Second-Premolar Hyrax Anchorage Linked to More Skeletal Expansion in CBCT Study
html:
Anchoring a tooth-borne Hyrax rapid maxillary expander on the second premolars and first molars was associated with greater skeletal expansion than anchoring it on the first premolars and first molars, according to a retrospective CBCT study published Nov. 18 in BMC Oral Health.

The single-center study included 52 patients ages 11–14, with 26 in each anchorage group. Investigators compared cone beam computed tomography scans taken before expansion and after three to six months of retention, measuring skeletal, dental, periodontal, and upper airway changes.

The second-premolar group showed greater increases in maxillary basal width, with a median difference of 1.25 mm. It also showed greater alveolar width at the second premolars and greater opening of the midpalatal suture in its anterior, middle, and posterior regions. Among dental measures, only second-premolar interapical width differed significantly after correction for multiple comparisons, with a median difference of about 2.4 mm.

The greater expansion was accompanied by more buccal bone plate thinning at the second premolars, a median difference of about 0.76 mm. Palatal bone plate thickening was greater at the first premolars with first-premolar anchorage and at the second premolars with second-premolar anchorage.

No upper airway measure differed significantly between the two designs. None of the exploratory correlations or regression models remained significant after adjustment.

The authors concluded that the findings may inform individualized anchorage selection but require prospective confirmation.

Xiaoli Guo, Baocheng Cao, and colleagues at Lanzhou University in China conducted the study.

Anchorage was not randomly assigned. The authors noted that nonrandom selection, residual confounding, CBCT measurement limitations, and short follow-up limit causal and clinical interpretation of the results.

Sources:
BMC Oral Health, “Skeletal, dental, periodontal, and upper airway changes after Hyrax rapid maxillary expansion with different premolar anchorage: a retrospective CBCT study,” published online Nov. 18, 2026: link.springer.com/10.1186/s12903-026-10453-9
